senses.definition: To relax; to spend time lazily; to stand, sit, or recline, in an indolent manner.
senses.example: We like to spend our Sundays lounging about at home in our pyjamas.

senses.definition: To walk or go in a leisurely manner.
senses.example: When this bejewelled exquisite lounged through the streets playing on his flute, puffing at a cigar, and smelling at a nosegay, the people whom he met threw themselves on the earth before him and prayed to him with sighs and tears.

senses.definition: A place where one can lounge; an area, establishment, house etc. where loungers gather and where one can relax and be at ease.
senses.example: He […] prevailed on Captain Musgrave to introduce him to a family, where he supposed he might find a monstrous good lounge for the rest of the time he was to be quartered in the neighbourhood.

senses.definition: The act of someone who lounges; idle reclining.
senses.example: That is, he devoted his waking hours to lounges among the habitués of Chestnut-street, and lollings in an arm-chair of 'Squire Coke in Walnut-street.

senses.definition: A room of a house for casual relaxing and entertaining.
senses.example: Near-synonyms: den, living room, sitting room, parlour, parlor, rec room

senses.definition: A large comfortable seat for two or three people or more, a sofa or couch; also called lounge chair.
A waiting room in an office, airport etc.
An establishment, similar to a bar, that serves alcohol and often plays background music or shows television.
senses.example: Near-synonyms: bar, pub, divan; see also Thesaurus:pub
